item.description: After 15 years, a Syrian man reopened the wall hiding his treasured library.?❤️ In 2011, Abu Bilal sealed hundreds of books, manuscripts, certificates and personal papers behind a concrete wall in his Homs home before leaving Syria. When he returned in 2026, he broke through the wall and found the collection still remarkably preserved. Fifteen years later, opening those shelves brought back not just books, but part of a life left behind.

item.title: GovBrief Today #601
item.description: Police in Springfield, Missouri, handcuffed a woman at Monday night's city council meeting and ticketed her for a disturbance, listing the evidence as "middle finger to mayor." She came to speak against the city's 41 Flock license plate cameras, but the council had just voted to shelve a review of them and cancel public comment on the subject. She raised it anyway, during comment on a housing bill. Her microphone went dead, and she kept speaking with both middle fingers in the air until police led her out. Two days later, a prosecutor in Indianapolis charged five current and former police officers with using their department's Flock cameras to track exes and spouses. One, an 18-year veteran, is charged with stalking women he met around town, including one from his workout class. The department caught them by checking who ran each search and why, the kind of review Springfield's council wouldn't let its residents talk about. item.title: First can you do me a favor.. Hold up 3 fingers in front of your face for me real quick.He froze. Didn't move..
item.description: A developer believes they unmasked a fake recruiter using a deepfake with a simple request: "Hold up three fingers in front of your face." During a supposed interview for a blockchain project, the person on the other end asked the developer to clone a GitHub repository and run it on their computer before proceeding with the technical interview. Suspicious, the developer agreed but first asked the recruiter to hold up three fingers in front of their face. The man froze for a few seconds, the call cut out, and the developer was blocked. He suspected the use of an AI-generated or AI-altered face. This story highlights a scam that has become particularly dangerous in the crypto ecosystem: fake recruiters approach developers with a credible offer before asking them to run a GitHub project supposedly required for a technical test. In reality, the repository may contain malware designed to steal passwords, private keys, cookies, or wallet access. https://x.com/costa__io/status/2102763033755791644

item.title: Feeling the goodness of the burn…
item.description:
In my previous post, I shared a hilarious video of an orchestra eating hot chili peppers before playing. Link: https://imgur.com/gallery/i-suppose-that-s-one-way-to-spice-up-performances-EnsxrWR . This actually made me curious about the flavor of spice. We can recognize flavors like sweet, salt, savory, and bitter, but spice is just… burn. I was curious because something that I noticed is that spice doesn’t have a real flavor. You can’t pick it out when it’s added to a food until it starts to burn. That’s the only real sign that spice is there. Why is that? It’s because spice isn’t actually a real flavor - it’s a physical sensation.
Here’s the article that explains the particulars. Don’t worry, I’ll summarize this better.
There’s really not much more to say on it. The brain thinks the mouth is on fire, and then in the process of trying to put it out, it ends up making the pain feel good. Except for me. My digestive tract is so sensitive to spice that I found myself in the ER from internal bleeding in my intestines due to Indian food. Good times.
I never heard of ice cream being used to soothe spice burn. That’s super interesting! . EDIT: Do not CHUG milk. That will not only waste milk, but hurt your stomach. Take a sip and swirl it around in your mouth. I was focusing more on making this lighthearted, and I didn’t really pay attention to what I was actually saying. My bad.
This is purely speculation on my end. I couldn’t find anything confirming or denying it. Anyway, I hope you enjoyed this post!
Spice Article from the Screenshots: https://sciencefocus.hkust.edu.hk/understand-spiciness-a-pain-but-not-a-taste A Second Overview of Spice: https://www.pfizer.com/news/articles/bodily_functions_explained_spicy_food_reaction Another Overview of Spicy Food: https://www.acs.org/education/celebrating-chemistry-editions/2025-ncw/the-science-of-hot-sauce-what-makes-it-spicy.html For Those Curious About Depolarization (heads up, it involves a lot of chemistry): https://eprojects.isucomm.iastate.edu/314-4-kbcm/2016/11/14/depolarization/
